item.title: Morse-Maxwell Theory for Directed Acyclic Graph
item.description: arXiv:2610.36372v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Maxwell graph of a directed acyclic graph is obtained from its iterated basin and hill boundaries. The unweighted counts of extrema at these levels need not satisfy Morse inequalities. We assign multiplicities by the reduced homology of lower and upper order links and retain the vertices with nonzero local homology. The resulting graph preserves both boundary hierarchies, the local groups, and the homology of all sublevel and superlevel order complexes. Its descending and ascending Morse numbers satisfy the weak and strong Morse inequalities over any field. We also construct a Morse chain complex and compute the local groups in several examples. Finally, we consider homology on the original Maxwell graph and prove analogous inequalities for path homology using relative local groups.
item.dc:creator: Oleg R. Musin

item.title: A minimising principle for interval covers of zigzag persistence modules
item.description: arXiv:2610.36843v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Zigzag persistence modules serve as an essential tool in topological data analysis. The fundamental theorem of persistent homology states that any zigzag persistence module decomposes into a direct sum of simple building blocks called interval modules. We consider an interval cover, a possibly redundant family of interval submodules spanning every vertex space of a finite zigzag persistence module. We give an elementary descent argument that replaces a redundant cover with a minimal one that is an interval decomposition. This provides an optimisation perspective on persistence modules and their interval decomposition. As an application, we give an estimate of the generalised rank invariant in terms of a cover.
item.dc:creator: Junyan Chu, Shizuo Kaji, Meiyan Kang

item.title: Homotopy operations on higher Lie algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.36942v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the multiplicative structures of the homotopy operations on derived Lie algebras, derived restricted Lie algebras and partition Lie algebras, as well as the relation between these. Under Koszul duality, this follows from a calculation of the homotopy operations on derived rings, p-truncated algebras and divided power algebras over $\mathbb{F}_p$.
item.dc:creator: Joost Nuiten, Jiaqi Fu

item.title: Countable models of one-dimensional Peano continua
item.description: arXiv:2610.35875v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we prove that a one-dimensional Peano continuum $X$ admits a weak homotopy equivalence $X\to C$ to a countable space $C$ if and only if the wild set $\mathbf{w}(X)$ is countable.
item.dc:creator: Jeremy Brazas, Petar Pavesic

item.title: Sheaves on polynomials and polynomial sheaves
item.description: arXiv:2610.36314v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that several Dold-Kan type equivalences can be understood as a passage from constructible sheaves on symmetric products (i.e. spaces of polynomials) to polynomial sheaves in the sense of Goodwillie-Weiss calculus, by means of a natural analytic expansion functor. This geometric perspective provides access to standard tools from sheaf theory such as the six functor formalism and $t$-structures. For example, the equivalence between filtered objects and coherent chain complexes in a stable $\infty$-category receives a geometric incarnation as Verdier duality between $!$-sheaves and $*$-cosheaves on an $\infty$-dimensional simplex. As a main application, we obtain an intrinsic geometric explanation for the appearance of vanishing cycle data for perverse sheaves in a paracyclic variant of the Dold--Kan correspondence pioneered by Dwyer and Kan, at the same time lifting their equivalence to stable $\infty$-categories.
item.dc:creator: Tobias Dyckerhoff, Till Heine, Simon Schneider

item.title: Topology of rational equivalence closures and Lawson homology
item.description: arXiv:2610.36913v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rational equivalence need not be closed in the Chow topology, and its closure can have infinitely generated homotopy groups. For a connected reduced complex projective variety, we prove that this closure is locally contractible and that its quotient in the algebraically trivial cycles is a finite or countable weak product of circles. The quotient map admits a global continuous section. Consequently, the higher homotopy of the cycle space is carried by the closure and is canonically identified with Lawson homology. We describe the remaining fundamental group quotient and its integral Walker comparison. Applications include smooth projective examples with infinite rank closure homotopy throughout prescribed finite intervals and a family of abelian threefolds with four simultaneously dense, nonconstructible quotient rank strata.
item.dc:creator: Wenchuan Hu

item.title: Localization, cobordism, and twisted $\chi_y$-genera of $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.37628v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We use the method of equivariant localization to obtain a recursion for the cobordism-valued one-point psi-class intersections on $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}$, and hence the cobordism classes $[\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}]$. Restricting to the hyperbolic formal group law, we recover the Poincar\'{e} polynomials of $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}$ as a special case, and obtain new formulas for Hirzebruch $\chi_y$-genera of $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}$ twisted by tautological line bundles.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Ellis-Bloor

item.title: On the rank of the double cohomology of moment-angle complexes
item.description: arXiv:2404.06763v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In [6], the authors construct a cochain complex $C\!H^*(\mathcal{Z}_{\mathcal{K}})$ on the cohomology of a moment-angle complex $\mathcal{Z}_{\mathcal{K}}$ and call the resulting cohomology the double cohomology, $H\!H^*(\mathcal{Z}_{\mathcal{K}})$. In this paper, we study the change of rank in double cohomology after gluing an $n$-simplex to a simplicial complex $\mathcal{K}$ in certain conditions. As an application, we give a positive answer to an open problem in [6]: For any even integer $r$, there always exists a simlicial complex $\mathcal{K}$ such that $\operatorname{rank} H\!H^*(\mathcal{Z}_{\mathcal{K}})=r$.
item.dc:creator: Zhilei Zhang, Linan Zhong

item.title: Limit Computation Over Posets via Minimal Initial Functors
item.description: arXiv:2601.00209v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It is well known that limits can be computed by restricting along an initial functor, and that this often simplifies limit computation. We systematically study the algorithmic implications of this idea for diagrams indexed by a poset. We say an initial functor $F\colon C\to D$ with $C$ small is minimal if the sets of objects and morphisms of $C$ each have minimum cardinality, among the sources of all initial functors with target $D$. For $Q$ a finite poset or $Q\subseteq \mathbb N^d$ an interval (i.e., a convex, connected subposet), we describe all minimal initial functors $F\colon P\to Q$. In particular, we show that such $F$ is always a subposet inclusion, up to isomorphism. We give efficient algorithms to compute a choice of minimal initial functor. In the case that $Q\subseteq \mathbb N^d$ is an interval, we give asymptotically optimal bounds on $|\hom P|$, the number of relations in $P$ (including identities), in terms of the number $n$ of minima of $Q$: We show that $|\hom P|=\Theta(n)$ for $d\leq 3$, and $|\hom P|=\Theta(n^2)$ for $d>3$. We apply these results to give new bounds on the cost of computing $\lim G$ for a functor $G \colon Q\to \mathbf{Vec}$ valued in vector spaces. For $Q$ connected, we also give new bounds on the cost of computing the generalized rank of $G$ (i.e., the rank of the induced map $\lim G\to \operatorname{colim} G$), which is of interest in topological data analysis.
item.dc:creator: Tamal K. Dey, Michael Lesnick

item.title: Equivariant formality and representation theory
item.description: arXiv:2609.00448v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G$ be a compact connected Lie group and $K$ its connected Lie subgroup. Using the $K$-theoretic version of equivariant formality developed in [F2] which involves analysis of vector bundles over $G/K$, we find two characterizations of equivariant formality of the isotropy action of $K$ on $G/K$. The first one equates equivariant formality with a "smoothness" condition of the restriction map of the representation ring of $G$ to that of $K$. The second characterization asserts that equivariant formality amounts to the equivariant $K$-theoretic index pairing of two certain special $K$-theory classes being nontrivial in some sense. By applying these characterizations, we are able to give a representation theoretic criterion for equivariant formality of the isotropy action by a circle subgroup, as well as an invariant theory criterion for the case where $K$ is a torus of dimension one less than the rank of $G$, culminating in a complete classification of equivariant formality where $G$ is further assumed to be simple.
item.dc:creator: Chi-Kwong Fok

item.title: Critical Diameters and Vietoris-Rips Filtrations
item.description: arXiv:2609.33009v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We relate critical diameters of finite configurations to the topology of Vietoris-Rips complexes. For a compact metric space and $0<r<s$, we prove that the canonical inclusion from scale $r$ to scale $s$ is a homotopy equivalence whenever $[r,s)$ contains no diameter of a finite labelled configuration at which the diameter function has zero weak slope. On Riemannian manifolds, weak-slope stationarity implies Clarke criticality. At positive diameter, when the distances realizing the diameter are smooth, both are equivalent to first-order stationarity: the absence of a direction decreasing all these distances to first order. For closed connected smooth manifolds, the Clarke critical diameter spectrum has Hausdorff dimension zero, even at the cut locus. In the real-analytic case, it is finite at each fixed number of labels and countable over all label numbers. On the unit round sphere $S^m$, $m\geq1$, positive nonantipodal weak-slope stationary configurations are characterized by nonzero nonnegative equilibrium stresses. The least positive critical diameter is $\arccos(-1/(m+1))$, and the first accumulation point is $\arccos(-1/m)$. We lift every such stress through a spherical stack construction adapted from Lov\'asz, producing stationary diameters that approach the original value from below in the next dimension as the number of layers increases. We also give example in general metric space showing that weak-slope stationary diameters need not correspond to changes in the homotopy type of Vietoris-Rips complexes.
item.dc:creator: Facundo M\'emoli, Qingsong Wang

item.title: The Art of Toda Brackets-A Journey through the Homotopy Groups of SO(n) in degrees 23-29
item.description: arXiv:2610.28447v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This book has several fundamental aims, one of which is to serve as a reference book for computing unstable homotopy groups using methods of the Toda school. The Toda bracket serves the art of constructing homotopy liftings and extensions of maps. It plays a fundamental role in dealing with composition relations of homotopy classes. This book brings together in Appendix A.3 all known results on the $2$-primary components of unstable homotopy groups of spheres obtained using the art of Toda brackets as the principal tool, with explicit generators. It also explains in Appendix A.2 the conventions used to name the generators. The book mainly presents calculations of the $2$-primary components of the homotopy groups $\pi_i(\mathit{SO}(n))$ for all $23\leq i\leq 28$ and all $n,$ as well as some $\pi_{29}(\mathit{SO}(n)),$ with explicit generators, while retaining two possible group structures for $\pi_{28}(\mathit{SO}(11)).$ In degree $29,$ the cases $7\leq n\leq14$ remain under investigation. The odd-primary components of the homotopy groups $\pi_i(\mathit{SO}(n))$ in the above range can be computed with little effort; these computations essentially amount to looking up the relevant entries in existing tables.
item.dc:creator: Yoshihiro Hirato, Jin-ho Lee, Toshiyuki Miyauchi, Juno Mukai, Mariko Ohara, Juxin Yang

item.title: The double of a simplicial complex
item.description: arXiv:2506.10436v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce the notion of doubling and r-tupling for simplicial complexes, a notion reminiscent to that of matching complexes in graph theory. We prove a connectivity result for such complexes and relate r-tupling to stabilizing r times faster in homological stability.
item.dc:creator: Kathryn Lesh, Bridget Schreiner, Nathalie Wahl

item.title: Some notes on tensor triangular geometry
item.description: arXiv:2602.08480v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: These are notes from the lectures I gave at the Oberwolfach seminar `Tensor Triangular Geometry and Interactions' which was held in October 2025. The aim of these notes is to give an introduction to tensor triangular geometry, for both small and large categories, through the lens of lattice theory. We do not try to be exhaustive and this is reflected in both the content and the bibliography. For instance we are quite light on triangulated preliminaries, especially for compactly generated categories. The first three sections treat the essentially small case and conclude with a tensor triangular proof of Thomason's theorem computing the spectrum of the perfect complexes on a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. The last section treats the compactly generated case. This final section is somewhat experimental and contains some new thoughts.
item.dc:creator: Greg Stevenson

item.title: Understanding Non-Split 2-Group Symmetry: (3+1)D SymTFT, Anomaly and Bordism
item.description: arXiv:2608.08766v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a systematic study of finite, non-split 2-group symmetries with a non-trivial Postnikov class, focusing on the simplest example with a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ 0-form symmetry and a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ 1-form symmetry, intertwined together by the non-trivial Postnikov class in $H^3(B\mathbb{Z}_2;\mathbb{Z}_2)\cong\mathbb{Z}_2$, denoted by $\mathcal{G}$. We classify the anomalies of this 2-group symmetry for physical theories in $d$-dimensional spacetime, by computing the oriented bordism groups $\Omega_{d+1}^{\rm SO}(B\mathcal{G})$ and the spin bordism groups $\Omega_{d+1}^{\rm Spin}(B\mathcal{G})$ for $d\leq 5$. For the case of $d=3$, we investigate the Symmetry TFT/TO of the 2-group symmetry $\mathcal{G}$ using the language of fusion 2-categories, as well as (3+1)D TQFT actions, for the cases without or with the 2-group anomaly classified by $\operatorname{Hom}\left(\widetilde{\Omega}_4^{\rm SO}(B\mathcal{G}),U(1)\right) \cong H^4(B\mathcal{G};U(1))\cong\mathbb{Z}_2$. We classify the minimal topological and physical boundary conditions of the Symmetry TFTs, and carry out the categorical Landau paradigm for such a non-split finite 2-group.
item.dc:creator: Zhenbang Gu, Ran Luo, Yi-Nan Wang, Yi Zhang
